Two of the three changes are fine. Removing `hours %= 24` matches the docstring ("not wrapped at 24"). Zero-padding the minutes (`{mins:02d}m`) is also correct.

The switch from `seconds // 60` to `round(seconds / 60)` needs to be reverted. The agent says in the PR description that it made this change only so `test_ninety_minute_session` would pass, and that it goes against the docstring: "leftover seconds are dropped, never rounded up". The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth. With this change, 5399s (1h 29m 59s) shows as "1h 30m" when it should show "1h 29m". It also rounds up in other places, for example 30s now shows as "1m" instead of "0m". Also, `round()` uses banker's rounding, so values that land exactly on a half-minute round inconsistently.

To fix: go back to truncation (`minutes = seconds // 60`). Keep the other two fixes. Bring the conflict between `test_ninety_minute_session` and the docstring to the teammate instead of changing code to match the test. Either the test's expected value is wrong, or the docstring needs updating, and that's their decision. A failing test is better than silently changing documented behavior to get a green run.
